sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Federal Rule of Evidence 704(b). The rule restricts expert opinions on a defendant's mental state. The parties disagree on whether this ban covers general class-based testimony.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to reject the Ninth Circuit's narrow reading of Rule 704(b).
The government wants the Court to uphold the rule's plain text limitation.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the rule bars any testimony allowing a jury to infer the defendant's mental state.
The government argues the rule only applies when experts explicitly opine on the defendant's own mental state.
